title: Clay vs Apollo vs Orange Slice for Signal-Based Outbound
summary: Clay vs Apollo vs Orange Slice for signal-based outbound: data, signals, pricing checked Oct 2026, and when each tool is the right pick.
body_markdown:
## Apollo for signal-based outbound


Apollo's strength is having data and sending in one place. You filter its database, add contacts to sequences, and call from the built-in dialer. It has a free plan, then per-user plans (Basic, Professional, Organization) billed annually; Organization requires three seats. An email costs 1 credit and a phone number 8 credits, and credits don't roll over. Apollo offers MCP on every plan ([apollo.io/product/mcp](https://www.apollo.io/product/mcp) ). Details and sources are on our[Orange Slice vs Apollo](https://www.orangeslice.ai/compare/apollo) page.


**Pick Apollo when:**


- You want one tool for finding contacts, sequencing and calling.
- Your targeting fits database filters (title, industry, size, location).
- You have several reps who each need a seat with a dialer.


**Watch out for:** signals that need custom research, like what a job description says or whether a site mentions a specific use case, are outside what a database filter does.


## Orange Slice for signal-based outbound


Orange Slice is an agentic enrichment spreadsheet ([what that means](https://www.orangeslice.ai/blog/what-is-an-agentic-enrichment-spreadsheet) ). You describe the signal and the list, for example "B2B SaaS companies under 200 people that posted a first RevOps role in the last 30 days, with the VP Sales and a verified email." The agent finds careers pages, reads postings, picks the buyer and runs a cheapest-first email waterfall. It works in a sheet, chat, API, CLI and MCP, pushes to HubSpot, Salesforce or Attio, and "sends invites, messages and follow-ups from your connected inbox and LinkedIn account," with optional review of every message ([homepage](https://orangeslice.ai/) ).


**Pricing (Oct 30, 2026):** Pay as you go is $0/month with a card, at vendor cost plus 25%. Pro is $99/month with $50 of usage, no markup on vendor cost, and a 7-day trial. Agency is $499/month with $250 of usage and a workspace per client. A work email costs up to $0.11 and nothing on a miss ([pricing](https://www.orangeslice.ai/pricing) ).


**Pick Orange Slice when:**


- Your best signals need research, not just filters.
- You don't have a GTM engineer and don't want to learn a table builder.
- You want to pay per lookup rather than per seat or per platform tier.
- Your team works in Claude Code or other agents.


**Watch out for:** no free plan, no SOC 2 audit yet, and a smaller provider catalog than Clay's.


## Can you use them together?


Yes, and many teams do. Common combinations:


- **Orange Slice or Clay for research, Apollo for sending.** Build the signal list in a sheet, then push contacts to Apollo sequences.
- **Clay for core workflows, Orange Slice for one-off research lists.** Use the agent for a quick question your Clay tables don't cover.
- **Apollo alone** while targeting is simple, then add a research tool once timing signals matter more than filters.


If none of the three fits, our list of[12 Clay alternatives](https://www.orangeslice.ai/blog/clay-alternative-lead-enrichment-prospecting) covers Databar, Freckle, Unify, Origami, TheirStack, PredictLeads and more. For seed-stage budgets, see[Clay alternative for YC startups](https://www.orangeslice.ai/blog/clay-alternative-for-yc-startups) .


## FAQ


### Is Clay or Apollo better for signal-based outbound?


Clay is better if your signals need custom workflows across many providers and you have someone to build them. Apollo is better if your targeting fits database filters and you want data, sequences and a dialer in one tool. Orange Slice suits teams that want research-heavy signals without building the workflow themselves.


### How much do Clay and Apollo cost in 2026?


On Oct 30, 2026, Clay listed a Free plan, Launch at $185 a month billed monthly or $167 billed annually, and Growth at $495 or $446. Apollo has a free plan, then per-user plans starting with Basic at $49 per user per month billed annually, per its pricing page as read on Oct 24, 2026.


### Does Orange Slice replace Apollo?


Sometimes. Orange Slice finds and verifies contacts and has email and LinkedIn sequences with review, so a small team may not need Apollo. Teams that rely on Apollo's dialer, its per-rep seats or its database filters often keep Apollo for sending and use Orange Slice to build signal-based lists.


### Which tool has the most data?


Clay connects to 150+ providers, Apollo runs its own large contact database, and Orange Slice routes across 40+ data vendors plus web research. Breadth isn't the same as accuracy for your market, so test each on the same 100 accounts and compare verified emails and useful signals before you decide.


### Do Clay, Apollo and Orange Slice support MCP?


Yes, according to their own pages as of October 2026. Apollo offers MCP on every plan, Clay lists a CLI, API and MCP, and Orange Slice runs through MCP and a CLI, including inside Claude Code. Check each vendor's docs for which actions the MCP server supports.
